One of the most common items transferred under this program was the Sherman M4 tank, and when it was presented to the public in a radio address, FDR likened it to the offer of a hose to a neighbor whose house was on fire without asking for payment in advance. FTP what was this program allowing the US to supply war materiel to the British and later the Russians before it officially entered WWII?

Newspaper editor L.A. Martinet arranged for the action that led to this court case, raising money for New York lawyer Albion Tourgee to represent the person selected to test the law. A first test involving the arrest of Daniel Desdunes was arranged, but after Desdunes was acquitted due to application of the interstate commerce clause of the Constitution, a purely in-state test was arranged. A woman was planted to make the complaint against the subject, as his status was not visibly clear due to his self-described 7/8 Caucasian heritage. Purchasing a ticket to Covington from New Orleans and sitting in a white car led to, FTP, the arrest of the plaintiff in what Supreme Court case of 1892 which upheld the concept of separate but equal facilities for African- Americans?

This is the only state in the U.S. Whose official motto is in Spanish, and it was the site of the "War of the Copper Kings," which left its institutions under the control of Marcus Daly's Anaconda Company. This home of Chief Dull Knife College, Stonechild College, and the University of Great Falls gets its news from such papers as the Missoulian, and the Daily Chronicle, published in Bozeman. The chief universities of this state, where the Battle of the Little Bighorn took place, have campuses in Billings and Butte. FTP name this state between North Dakota and Idaho, known as "Big Sky Country."

His final tournament victory came in 2005 in Los Angeles over Gilles Muller. He lost his first major final to Andres Gomez at the 1990 French Open and eventually won the tournament in 1999, coming back from two sets down to defeat Andre Medvedev, which made him the fifth person to earn a career Grand Slam. This star of Canon Camera ads in which he smugly stated, "Image is everything" recently admitted to a brief life tailspin which included using crystal meth, though since then he has married Steffi Graf. FTP name this tennis star, the rival of Pete Sampras.

This Ohio politician served as Treasury Secretary under Hayes and had his campaign for the Republican nomination for president derailed when his own campaign manager, James Garfield, was selected as a dark horse candidate. One piece of legislation associated with his name increased currency circulation and supplanted the Bland-Allison Act until it was repealed in 1893, while another he sponsored was first invoked against the American Railway Union in order to put down the Pullman Strike. FTP who was this Ohio senator whose fame rests on namesake Silver Purchase and Anti-Trust Acts?

Ted Joans, called by Andre Breton the only African-American Surrealist, is better associated with this other literary group. Poet Michael McClure, who recorded the spoken-word CD "There's a Word!" with Ray Manzarek, is also associated with this group of writers. The long poems "Gasoline" and "Bomb" are representative of this movement, as is the novel Go! By John Clellon Holmes, who also published the first article to use the movement's name, quoting a comment made by the author of Satori in Paris and Dr. Sax. Epitomized by authors like Gregory Corso and William S. Burroughs, FTP what is this literary movement of the 1950s and 60s most associated with Allen Ginsburg and Jack Kerouac?

The Sogdian people revolted against this empire when it revoked its promise not to tax them if they converted, highlighting its problems with tax expectations on non-Arab Muslims. Its first dynasty within a dynasty was called the Sufyanids, and its founder ended the First Fitnah. Its last Caliph, Marwan II, died, Abd ar-Rahman I was the only of their line to escape, fleeing to Spain where the Caliphate continued. By the time that the Abbasids had killed Marwan II, this empire extended from Spain to India. FTP identify this Islamic dynasty, founded by Muawiyya, the first Islamic caliphate.

Dionysus escaped capture from King Lycurgus by taking refuge in this woman's grotto. Medea unsuccessfully competed with this figure in a beauty contest judged by Idomeneus, and she got the hundred-handed figure Briareus to release Zeus. Along with Eurynome, she rescued Hephaestus after he was dropped from Olympus by Hera. At this woman's wedding, the uninvited Eris brought a golden apple with the inscription "To the Fairest." She burned alive her first six sons, but her husband, Peleus, saved the seventh and sent that son to be raised by the centaur Chiron, but not before she dipped that son in the waters of the Styx. FTP name this Nereid, the mother of Achilles.

Most non-battle-related casualties from this war stemmed from an outbreak of yellow fever and Russell Alger's decision to supply troops with spoiled meat, leading to the "Embalmed Beef" scandal. One front of this war was commanded by William Shafter, who ordered the attack on El Caney, while a far- away front was commanded by George Dewey. Its best-known land battle saw cavalry led by Leonard Wood charge up Kettle Hill. FTP name this 1898 conflict which included the American victory at the Battle of Manila Bay and was triggered by the explosion of the USS Maine.

This man used an almanac to prove William "Duff" Armstrong's innocence in one case. In the House of Representatives, he demanded to know the exact location where blood had been spilled on American soil by the Mexican army in his "Spot Resolutions." This man spoke out against the Kansas-Nebraska Act in his Peoria Speech. This man suggested advancing "With malice toward none, with charity for all" in his Second Inaugural Address. This politician debated Stephen A. Douglas during a 1858 senate race. FTP name this Republican who delivered the Gettysburg Address as president during the Civil War.

One of the lasting effects of his reign was the complete and utter destruction of the Pecheneg nomads to the north of the Danube. He also fended off an attack from the Normans led by Robert Guiscard, retook quite a bit of the Anatolian coastline, and founded a lasting Byzantine dynasty. FTP identify this emperor, whose deeds were chronicled by his daughter Anna, who may be best known for sending a letter to Urban II that inadvertently invited the First Crusade.

In 2007 15 British soldiers were captured by another nation for allegedly infringing on that nation's claims in this body of water. Cities lying on this body of water include Al Manamah and Busheher. The body of water that drains it is named for Ahura Mazda. The Shatt al-Arab empties two large rivers into it at the city of Abadan. Islands in it include Tarout, Kish, and Bahrain. FTP identify this body of water that drains into the Gulf of Oman via the Strait of Hormuz, along which lie the nations of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and Iran.

This man met with Eisenhower at Morningside Heights, and agreed to back him in the 1952 presidential election despite their different opinions on NATO. He lost two nominations for president, the most contested of which went to his arch-rival Thomas Dewey. His criticism of ex post facto application of laws at the Nuremburg Trials led to JFK's "Profile in Courage" on this man, and he co-sponsored a labor relations law that replaced the Wagner Act, along with Fred Hartley. FTP name this so-called "Mr. Republican," a longtime Ohio senator and son of former president and Chief Justice William Howard.

This person lost an Assembly seat for criticizing the Paxton Boys' Affair, which prompted him to go on a diplomatic mission. During this mission on behalf of his adoptive home colony, he became the representative of Georgia, New Jersey, and Massachusetts, beginning to bring about the unification proposed in his failed Albany Plan of Union. Also the first Postmaster General of the United States, this was, what founding father associated with the lightning rod and Poor Richard's Almanac?

This person wrote Affairs of France and Germany after diplomatic missions in those countries. The highest political post this writer held was as secretary of the Ten before he was disgraced and tortured for his role in a conspiracy. In addition to the play Mandragola and Seven Books on the Art of War, he wrote a commentary of the Roman republic in his seminal Discourses on Livy. Howeve, he is more famous for the Florentine Histories and a 1532 work condemned by Pope Clement VIII that posits the benefits of a monarchical society. Identify this Italian political philosopher and author of The Prince.

Its more esoteric provisions forbade self-castration and prohibited priests from having young female houseguests. It dealt with when to celebrate Passover and attempted to mediate the Meletian schism. But its most important function was to settle a major conflict between the Homoousians and the Arians over the rightful place of the Son and the Father, resulting in a more uniform Church of Alexandria. Name this first ecumenical council convened by Constantine I in 325 that produced a namesake creed.

The attacking forces in this battle planned to drive the Federal Army to Owl Creek, a setting which may have inspired a title of noted combatant Ambrose Bierce, who also wrote a first-hand account entitled "What I saw of" this place. Fearing reinforcements led by Don Carlos Buell, the Confederate commander ordered a preemptive attack on Grant's forces, recently victorious at Forts Henry and Donelson. This attack resulted in a two-day battle near the Sunken Road that saw its heaviest action in the "Hornet's nest" and the death of A.S. Johnston in the defense of Pittsburg Landing. Name this April 6-7, 1862 Union victory fought in southwestern Tennessee.

Highly influenced by and revised due to Wilhelm Stekel, much of its discussion surrounds an incident known as "Irma's injection". Arguing that the title phenomena take place in stages of condensation, displacement, and finally secondary revision, it also seeks to differentiate between latent and manifest content, arguing that the preconscious suppresses the wish fulfillment from making its way to the conscious mind before waking up. Name this seminal 1900 work on analyzing reverie, written by Sigmund Freud.

This man is an author of The True Law of Free Monarchies, which articulated the divine right of kings, and of Basilikon Doron, where he listed sodomy as a "horrible crime" despite being a homosexual himself. Earlier, after his ship was caught in a storm, he believed witches caused it in order to kill him and wrote a treatise on demonology, which led to hundreds of his subjects killed for witchcraft. Name this English monarch, who succeeded Elizabeth I and whose reign included such notable events as the Guy Fawkes plot and the creation of his namesake version of the Bible.

This regions native residents are also known as Uryankhai. Briefly independent between the world wars, this autonomous republic with capital at Kyzyl is home to the headwaters of the Yenisey River. Name this principality south of Siberia, the subject of the 1999 documentary Genghis Blues, notable for its throat singing.

In 1937, this person chaired a commission of enquiry that cleared Trotsky of the charges brought against him in the Moscow Trials. This thinker's more philosophical works include Ethics, co-written by James Tufts, and The Quest for Certainty. He wrote about stimuli of the in "The Reflex Arc Concept in Psychology." This social scientist co-founded the New School for Social Research and the University of Chicago Laboratory Schools. Name this American pragmatist who may be best-known for the ideas espoused in Democracy and Education, namely those of progressive, scientific education.

Benjamin Butler represented some of the men convicted after this event, all of whom were later pardoned by John Peter Altgeld. Immediately preceded by a fight at the McCormick Harvesting Machine Co. At which four were killed by police, this event is commemorated by bonfires at some May Day celebrations. Name this tragedy that helped lead to the downfall of the Knights of Labor; a May 4th, 1886 riot touched off when someone detonated a bomb at a labor rally in Chicago.

Martin Luther notably mistranslated the name of the leader of one side in this engagement, which saw Numonius Vala flee after a failed assault on a wall at the foot of the Kalkriese Hill. The victorious commander would go on to be betrayed and murdered after defeating the Marcomanni ten years later, while the loser, Varus, committed suicide, prompting Augustus to demand his troops back. Name this 9 CE battle in which the Germanic forces, led by Arminius, ambushed and annihilated three Roman legions in a certain forest.

Asser's record of this man's life is a fine source, thought he ruled for six more years after its publication. This king's defeated his people's great rivals in the Battle of Eddington of 878, after which their king Guthrum converted to Christianity and settled in East Anglia. This man's most enduring work was the legal reforms codified in his Book of Dooms, which eventually grew into English Common Law, and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle began under his reign. Name this ruler notable for his scholarship and for defeating the Danes as the king of Wessex, which lead to his being given the epithet "the Great."

This person's older brother was made an honorary general in the Turkish army for opening the first Western music school in Constantinople. This man wrote the duet "Prender moglie!" for an opera about Ernesto and Norina marrying due to the machinations of Doctor Malatesta. In addition to Don Pasquale, his operas include La Favorite, The Daughter of the Regiment, and two operas about English queens, Maria Stuart and Anna Bolena. Name this composer of an opera based on a Walter Scott work, Lucia di Lamermoor, as well as the tale of a harmless bottle of wine, The Elixir of Love.

Solon learned the tale of Atlantis from a priest of this land, while Cadmus took the power of speech from this place. The ship-pilot Canobus died here during the wanderings of Menelaus and its king Proteus is often said to have hidden Helen here while a phantom double was sent to Troy. It was conquered from the Melampods by the son of Anchinoe and Belus, and the Curetes stole the newborn Epaphus after Io regained human form here. Name this land where the Hellenistic god Hermes Trismegestus was believed to reside and where the Greeks identified an aspect of Demeter with Isis.

This movement was not put down until Henry le Despenser defeated John Litster's army, long after it had targeted Fleet prison and Savoy palace. Some of its instigators grievances about the Statute of Laborers, but it executed Robert Hales and Simon of Sudbury for administering the one-shilling fee that nominally sparked it. Shortly after it rose out of Essex and Kent to challenge Richard II, its leader was killed in a scuffle with William Walworth, the mayor of London. Name this campaign against the poll tax of 1380 led by Wat Tyler.

Urban renewal in this city has focused on the Docklands neighborhood. It is the location of La Trobe, Deakin and Monash universities and its downtown is centered on the pedestrian malls of Bourke and Swanston. Extending east to Point Nepean, it is the southernmost metro area of more than a million residents in the world and is found where the Yarra River enters Port Phillip Bay. Name this southeastern Australian city, the capital of Victoria and the second-largest city in the country after Sydney.

This organization's leader for the Greenville area was the man who coined the phrase "great American novel," John DeForest. Created at the urging of Josephine Griffing and Edward Pierce, its operations followed the "Port Royal plan." Corruption by its local agents led to the 1874 court-martial of its commander, but had already of a new university in Washington and about a thousand other schools, the former named for that commander. Name this agency led by General Oliver Otis Howard which provided aid to former slaves during Reconstruction.
the Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands

A leader of one side in this conflict argued its necessity of by displaying figs to illustrate the enemy's apparent strength. Touched off by resistance to Masinissa, this war was put on a short hold when the defenders agreed to a surrender of arms and hostages, but they balked at a requirement to move inland. Ended when Scipio Aemilianus invaded from Sicily and undertook a successful three-year siege, this conflict began at the urging of Cato the Elder in 149 BCE. Identify this war that resulted in the destruction and enslavement of Carthage; the last in a series of conflicts between that city and Rome.
